explanation: Single body with e=0.5 falls onto floor (y=0) under gravity. At step 90 body is just above floor (y=0.798, vy=-18.34, energy ~176 J, within bound). At step 91 after floor collision, vy is +28.96 (speed 28.96) instead of expected ~+9 J with e=0.5 restitution (energy-conserving bounce should reduce speed). Energy jumps to 427.2 J, exceeding allowed 198.7 J (E0 176.08 +10%+5). No controller work. Indicates floor impulse/positional-correction bug that injects energy on restitution: bounce velocity magnitude exceeds incoming magnitude despite e<1 and gravity alone cannot explain gain. Counterfactual raising initial height to y=5 avoids floor impact within 91 steps and shows no violation, confirming collision handling is causal.
vision_note: Steps 88-90 show the blue body hovering just above the floor with minimal vertical change, and step 91 shows it still essentially in contact with the floor with no discernible upward displacement. There is no visible high-speed rebound or large jump between the pre-impact frame 90 and the post-impact frame 91. [disagreement: The numeric explanation claims an energy-injecting floor bounce at step 91 with vy flipping to +28.96 and total energy jumping from ~176 J to 427 J, which should appear as a dramatic upward launch. The image shows effectively static contact with no energetic bounce, so the visual does not corroborate the massive velocity/energy gain described.]
